title: "Anticoagulation and risk of silent cerebral ischemia during aneurysm embolization: two different heparin doses assessed by MRI" "HARMONI"
official: "Evaluation of the impact of the dose of heparin on the occurrence of DWI ischemic lesions after embolization of unruptured intracranial aneurysm" "HARMONI"
summary: Main objective: The primary objective is to compare the effect of two different heparin regimens, 30 IU/kg and 70 IU/kg, on the incidence of recent ischemic lesions detected by diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) on routine brain MRI performed 24 ± 12 hours after endovascular treatment of a saccular intracranial aneurysm, either unruptured or ruptured more than 30 days earlier.

interventions.name: HEPARINE SODIQUE PANPHARMA 5 000 UI/ml, solution injectable (I.V.)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Patient aged ≥ 18 years
2. Patient presenting with a saccular intracranial aneurysm, either unruptured or ruptured more than 30 days prior
3. Patient without neurological deficit
4. Pre-procedural mRS score < 3
5. Free and informed consent
6. Affiliated with or entitled to a social security scheme
Exclusion criteria:
1. Current anticoagulant treatment (Vitamin K antagonists, oral anticoagulants, curative heparin therapy) at the time of aneurysm embolization.
2. Any known pre-existing coagulopathy or bleeding disorder
3. Pregnant or breastfeeding women
4. Planned embolization of multiple aneurysms on different arterial axes during the same procedure (inclusion remain possible if multiple aneurysms are treated on the same arterial axis).
5. Obesity defined as body mass index (BMI) > 30
6. Poor understanding of the French language
7. Patient under legal protection (guardianship or curatorship)
8. Person unable to personally give consent
9. Person deprived of liberty by judicial or administrative decision
10. Other planned cervical or intracranial endovascular treatments during the same procedure (e.g., carotid stenting, embolization of a dural arteriovenous fistula, or a cerebral arteriovenous malformation, other).
11. Particularly complex endovascular access, such as severe cervical or intracranial atherosclerosis, major tortuosity of supra-aortic trunks, or sequelae of severe arterial dissection.
12. Stenting of the ipsilateral carotid artery within 3 months prior to the procedure.
13. Recent ischemic cerebral event (< 1 month) (TIA or stroke)
14. Subject who underwent surgery with hemorrhagic risk within 30 days prior to the study procedure
15. Intracranial hemorrhage and/or subarachnoid hemorrhage within 30 days prior to the study procedure.
16. Known history or suspected cerebral amyloid angiopathy.
17. Aneurysm associated with a cerebral arteriovenous malformation (AVM).
18. Patient with organic lesions associated with a risk of bleeding
19. Patient with end-stage renal disease or severe hepatic impairment
20. Contraindication to unfractionated heparin
21. Severe known allergy to radiographic contrast agents.
22. Known hypersensitivity to nickel, titanium, or their alloys
23. Concurrent participation in another clinical study that could interfere with the study’s outcome measures
24. Contraindication to MRI or angiography for any reason
25. Comorbid disease or condition that could affect neurological and functional assessments or compromise survival (significant sequelae of stroke or traumatic brain injury, advanced neurodegenerative disease, severe Parkinson’s disease, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, dementia, symptomatic or progressive brain tumour, multiple sclerosis or another neurological disorder causing fluctuating deficits, poorly controlled epilepsy, severe psychiatric disorder, documented confusion or cognitive impairment, advanced or metastatic active cancer, or severe infectious or systemic disease).
26. Known allergy to heparin, aspirin (ASA), or other antiplatelet agents
27. History of heparin-induced thrombocytopenia
